title: Experiment exposure event schema + telemetry ingestion (route-level A/B testing)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Background
We need a low-overhead, privacy-safe exposure logging path for route-level A/B experiments. This is the canonical dataset for (a) experiment reporting denominators (exposures by variant) and (b) audit/debug workflows when customers or Support dispute whether traffic was actually split as configured.

This ticket covers:
1) Exposure event schema (v1) + validation rules
2) Sampling policy + deterministic sampling implementation guidance
3) Ingestion pipeline changes (topic/table, validation, dedupe, partitioning)
4) Backfill plan / “data available since” behavior
5) Validation tests (unit/integration/load) + rollout checklist

Non-goals
- Arbitrary user-defined metrics ingestion.
- Quality/eval results schema (handled by eval harness integration).
- UI work / results dashboard queries (covered by ENG-2844/ENG-2845).

References
- ADR-0188: Experiment exposure logging and privacy (Confluence)
- Observability standard: ab-testing-metrics-schema-v1 (Confluence)
- Related implementation PRs:
  - redwood PR #18371 (emit exposure events from gateway)
  - redwood PR #18388 (telemetry pipeline ingest exposure events)

Requirements
Functional
- Ingest exposure events emitted at the API gateway for experiment-enabled routes.
- Enforce a strict allowlist for event fields/tags to prevent high-cardinality blowups.
- Provide stable event IDs to support deduplication for retries/stream reconnect.
- Support both Hosted + Dedicated routing paths.

Privacy/Security
- No raw PII (no email, IP, user-agent, prompt content, message content).
- No customer-provided headers except the explicitly documented assignment key header (hashed before emission).
- Tenant/project identifiers must be Redwood internal IDs (not customer strings).
- Access must be restricted to internal roles + aggregated customer-facing outputs.

Performance
- Gateway emission must be non-blocking; failure to emit must not fail the request.
- Ingestion must handle peak exposure volume at 2x expected beta partner traffic.

Event schema (experiment_exposure.v1)
Event type/name
- event_name: "experiment_exposure"
- schema_version: "1"

Identity + dedupe
- exposure_id: stable UUID-like string derived as sha256("v1" + experiment_id + assignment_key_hash + request_id) and hex/base64url encoded
  - used for idempotent ingest + at-least-once delivery
- request_id: Redwood request ID (already generated in gateway)
- trace_id: optional (if tracing enabled; must be sampled consistently with tracing)

Experiment dimensions (low-cardinality)
- experiment_id: stable experiment identifier (UUID)
- experiment_name: optional, truncated + validated (<= 64 chars); may be empty in beta to avoid rename churn
- variant_id: stable variant identifier (UUID)
- variant_name: required in Console, but in telemetry: optional string (<= 64) to avoid cardinality; preference is to use variant_id in aggregations
- allocation: string representation of configured split at time of exposure (e.g., "A:90,B:10"); optional; used only for debugging

Routing context
- route_id: internal route identifier (UUID) OR canonicalized string ("/v1/chat/completions") if UUID isn’t available end-to-end; must be from allowlist of known Redwood routes
- deployment_mode: "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private" (private allowed but may be gated)
- region: canonical region code (e.g., "us-east", "eu-west")
- cluster_id: optional; internal only; must be from allowlisted set (no free-form)

Customer context (internal IDs only)
- tenant_id: Redwood internal tenant UUID
- project_id: Redwood internal project UUID
- api_key_id: internal UUID; optional (allowed for debugging authentication-related skew)

Assignment inputs (hashed)
- assignment_key_type: "tenant" | "api_key" | "header" | "user"
- assignment_key_hash: sha256 of the raw key (salted with Redwood secret; produced at gateway)
  - NOTE: raw key MUST NOT be emitted

Timing
- timestamp_ms: epoch millis at time of assignment
- gateway_received_ms: optional; for diagnosing queueing vs compute

Outcome flags
- decision: "assigned" | "fallback" | "bypassed"
  - assigned: request was routed per experiment allocation
  - fallback: experiment eligible but routed via fallback policy due to guardrails/capacity
  - bypassed: not eligible (e.g., route mismatch, region not enabled, missing assignment key)
- reason_code: optional enum string ("missing_assignment_key", "experiment_paused", "region_not_enabled", "capacity_constrained", "policy_precedence", "validation_failed")

Strictly prohibited fields
- prompt/messages/content
- raw headers (except those already part of Redwood canonical request envelope)
- IP address / device identifiers

Sampling policy
We need two layers:
1) Aggregated metrics (counters/histograms) by experiment_id + variant_id are handled elsewhere and are NOT sampled.
2) Raw exposure events are sampled to limit storage cost and reduce risk surface.

Proposed default sampling for raw exposure events:
- base_sample_rate: 0.10 (10%) for "assigned" decisions
- sample_rate for "fallback" decisions: 1.0 (always) for the first 48h of beta per tenant, then 0.25 after (to preserve debug signal when reliability issues occur)
- sample_rate for "bypassed": 0.01 (only for diagnosing eligibility/config issues)

Sampling MUST be deterministic:
- sampled = (xxhash64(experiment_id + request_id) mod 10000) < (sample_rate * 10000)
- ensures stable sampling under retries/replays and supports comparing across pipelines

Ingestion / storage
- Add new event stream/topic: telemetry.events.experiment_exposure
- Persist to warehouse table: telemetry_experiment_exposure_v1
  - partition by date (timestamp_ms) and region
  - cluster/sort by experiment_id, tenant_id
- Dedupe on (exposure_id) within a 7-day window (late arrivals expected)
- Enforce schema validation:
  - reject events with unknown fields
  - hard limits on string length
  - enum validation for deployment_mode/decision/reason_code
  - route_id must be allowlisted OR match a small regex set for known Redwood endpoints
- PII scanning: add rule to block/alert if any field matches IP/email patterns (belt-and-suspenders)

Backfill plan
- No backfill for GA/beta reporting.
- Console reporting should display "Data available since" = first_ingested_timestamp for experiment_id (queryable in results service).
- Optional future enhancement (NOT in scope here): reconstruct approximate exposures from gateway access logs for a limited window; would require explicit privacy review.

Acceptance criteria
- Schema is documented + reviewed by Telemetry (Logan/Nadia) and Security (Marcus/Naomi).
- Ingestion pipeline accepts valid events and rejects invalid events with actionable errors.
- Dedupe prevents double-counting on gateway retries/stream reconnect.
- Sampling is deterministic and configurable via remote config (per tenant override) with sane defaults.
- End-to-end validation in staging: create experiment -> generate traffic -> verify events present, deduped, and partitioned correctly.
- Load test demonstrates ingestion keeps up with 2x expected beta partner QPS and stays within pipeline error budget.

Testing plan
- Unit tests
  - schema validation (happy path + unknown field + oversized strings + invalid enums)
  - sampling determinism (fixed seeds)
  - dedupe key stability
- Integration tests
  - staging canary producing synthetic exposure traffic
  - verify table row count approximates sample rate for assigned vs bypassed
- Data quality monitors
  - alert on sudden drop in exposures for active experiments (pipeline failure)
  - alert on spikes in unknown reason_code / bypassed (misconfig/regression)

Rollout plan
- Dark-launch ingestion with no downstream consumers.
- Enable for internal dogfood tenant at 10% sample.
- Expand to beta partners with per-tenant override if Support needs higher fidelity during onboarding.

Open questions
- Do we need api_key_id in v1? (Nadia requested for debugging skew; security wants to confirm it’s not considered sensitive in our model.)
- Should route_id be UUID-only (preferred) or allow canonical route strings in v1 until routing service propagates UUID?
- Retention: 14 days raw events vs 30 days. Proposal: 14 days raw, 90 days aggregates.
comments: 2026-02-05 (Logan Wright): Marking this as P0 for beta. Results dashboard needs a reliable denominator dataset + ability to audit "who saw what" at least at sampled granularity. Please sync schema choices with ADR-0188 before we bake it into gateway emission.

2026-02-07 (Caleb Johnson): Drafted schema v1 in the description. Key callout: deterministic sampling based on (experiment_id, request_id) and dedupe on exposure_id. Need confirmation from Routing on whether request_id is always present before assignment happens in gateway.

2026-02-10 (Nadia Rahman): +1 to include api_key_id (internal UUID) as optional. We’ve had prior incidents where auth tier / key rotation caused traffic skew; being able to filter exposures by api_key_id is useful. As long as it’s UUID-only and not customer-provided, I think this is safe.

2026-02-11 (Marcus Lin): Security review notes: (1) no raw header values; only salted hashes. (2) keep variant_name optional and capped; prefer variant_id in storage. (3) ensure PII scanner blocks common patterns even if schema is strict (defense-in-depth). OK with api_key_id as internal UUID.

2026-02-13 (Mina Haddad): Routing context: route UUID propagation is not end-to-end yet for Dedicated in all regions. Suggest we allow canonical route string for v1 (from a strict allowlist) and migrate to UUID-only later. Avoid free-form.

2026-02-17 (Caleb Johnson): Implementing ingestion with "unknown fields => reject" to prevent silent cardinality creep. Added plan to emit metrics on reject counts by reason (unknown_field, invalid_enum, oversize, pii_detected) so we can catch regressions quickly.

2026-02-20 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: we need an alert on exposure ingestion drop for active experiments, since the results UI will otherwise look "empty" and customers will assume split is broken. Please add a basic data freshness check (last_ingested_at by experiment_id) feeding into the experiment dashboards.

2026-02-24 (Caleb Johnson): Staging E2E test run: events are ingesting; dedupe working for forced retry replay. Noted mismatch between expected 10% and observed 12–13% due to hashing mod bug (off-by-one). Fix in progress; will update once merged.
